cases.name: built-in worked example
stdout: (no config - demo: one invented webinar planned backwards, its run-of-show, and the readout six weeks later)
PLAN - backwards from 150,000 of pipeline
Opportunities 10 -> meetings 20 -> live attendees 200 -> registrations 500
Cost 7,300 (people time 3,600): 15 per registration, 37 per attendee, 365 per meeting; 20.5 of pipeline per 1 spent
Weakest step: attendeeToMeetingRate - the rate most worth lifting.

STRETCH: You can reach 70% of the registrations needed. Either add a partner's audience, lower the target, or lift a rate you control (show rate through reminders; attendee-to-meeting through the offer).
RUN OF SHOW - 3 of 8 items missing
! Dry run done on the real platform: Audio, screen share, polls and the handoff between speakers, tested once.
! Follow-up sequence written before the event: Attendees, no-shows and on-demand viewers each get a different first email within a day.
! Sales handoff agreed: Who calls whom, within what time, on what signal (question asked, poll answer, stayed to the end).
READOUT - on meetings and pipeline, not registrations
320 registered, 121 attended live (38%), 64 on demand; 14 meetings, 6 opportunities, 84,000 pipeline
Cost 7,300: 60 per attendee, 39 per person reached, 521 per meeting, 1,217 per opportunity; 11.5 of pipeline per 1 spent; expected revenue 21,000
! First follow-up went out 44 hours after the event. AAJ's rule is within 24 hours; the follow-up is the real event.
CHANGE: Expected revenue (pipeline x win rate) is 2.9x cost: it pays for itself but misses your 3x target. Change the weakest step before running again.
